thread:
alex: noticed a p99 spike in SSE streaming on canary after last night's roll (~+12%). p50 looks fine, tail is inflated.
priya: confirmed on two customer routes too. CI flagged it on the streaming latency suite.
ci-bot: perf-ci: streaming-latency-suite failed on canary build 2026-03-15T18:12Z — p99 +12.3% vs baseline.
jamal: I ran a quick profile under load. user-space shows lots of short write syscalls (~700-1.2KB each). previously we saw ~6-10KB aggregated writes.
eva: which change landed yesterday?
alex: PR 2334 merged — "streaming: adjust flush trigger and toolcall framing" (merge abc1234) by linus.
linus: goal was to reduce latency for tiny frames by making flush trigger >64 bytes instead of >=64, and we also set TCP_NODELAY for the toolcall path. didn't expect tail to worsen.
priya: digging into serialized toolcall payloads — there's an extra 40-60B header per chunk now. combined with the earlier flush we end up emitting N small frames instead of a single coalesced frame.
jamal: bisect locally shows abc1234 correlates with the regression. reverting that commit locally drops p99 back to baseline.
ci-bot: perf-ci: automated bisect confirms: pre-abc1234 p99=baseline, post-abc1234 p99=+11%.
alex: tcpdump from repro: a burst of ~50 consecutive writes, many ~1kB. socket options show TCP_NODELAY enabled on the new path. prior behavior relied on kernel coalescing plus user-space aggregation to reach ~8KB writes.
eva: interaction with KV cache is subtle — high KV-hit shortens token outputs but toolcalls still produce many small frames; when KV misses increase we see different batching behavior. both paths now trigger many small writes.
linus: I missed the kv/toolcall interaction. my change reduced one latency class but regressed tail when combined with other behavior.
priya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) hold canary rollout; 2) revert PR 2334 in canary; 3) open hotfix restoring >=64 coalesce and keep tcp_nodelay consistent across streaming paths; 4) add perf test that asserts socket write count under high-kv-hit streaming. I'll open the hotfix PR now.
jamal: longer term: implement a configurable user-space coalescer that buffers small frames up to a target (4-8KB) unless the application explicitly marks a frame as immediate-flush. that prevents pathological small-write storms while preserving low-latency signals.
eva: also add a synthetic perf job that simulates interleaved toolcalls + KV-hits and checks p99 and write-counts. put it behind perf-ci so we catch regressions early.
linus: agree on coalescer + explicit flush flag in streaming header. I'll help spec the header flag and update runtime docs.
priya: adding flamegraph + tcpdump snippets to the hotfix PR for reviewers.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback triggered for roll/2026-03-15-c1.
deploy-bot: rollback completed to roll/2026-03-15-c0 — canary held.
oncall-bot: monitoring alert: SSE p99 > baseline +5% triggered; acknowledged and monitoring ramped up for 12h.
alex: good. after hotfix merges we should run a targeted latency stress job and a full perf-ci baseline.
jamal: note for postmortem: root cause = behavioral regression from coalesce threshold change combined with TCP_NODELAY toggle; mitigations = revert, hotfix coalescer, new perf tests, and a rollout checklist item to run KV/toolcall mix scenarios.
eva: tagging eng-runtime, eng-infra, and eng-ml for visibility. assigning postmortem owner once hotfix lands. :thumbsup:
priya: PR opened: hotfix/2334-revert-and-coalesce-test — linking perf traces and tcpdump. reviewers: jamal, linus, alex.
linus: will review now. sorry team, lesson learned on multidimensional perf effects.
alex: thanks everyone. monitoring and rollback done — keeping this as a rollout blocker until we see perf baseline restored.
